THESE APPEALS, ARE COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING,
THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.484/2016 dated 04.07.2017 on the file of the I Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Mandya.
Both the insurance company as well as the claimant are before this court.
The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is MFA.No.7692/2017 and appeal filed by the claimant is MFA.No.8748/2017.
The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.12,90,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident.
As per the wound certificate the claimant had sustained fracture of arch of zygoma left side.
As per the doctor the claimant had sustained functional disability at 30% and the Tribunal has considered 10% as the disability.

According to the claimant,
he is earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- and Tribunal had considered an amount of Rs.10,000/- as income and granted compensation of an amount of Rs.2,83,005/-.

3. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that when she has sustained such a grievous injury, for pain and suffering, for nourishment and for the future loss of income, the amounts granted by the Tribunal were not reasonable.
It is submitted that for the disfigurement, no amounts were granted by the Tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for the insurance company submits that though the claimant was earning an amount NC: 2023:KHC:46244 of Rs.10,000/- per month, though there is no evidence, still the court below had taken an amount of Rs.10,000/- as income and granted the compensation.
He submits that the facial disability will not have any impact on the future prospects, the court below ought not to have granted the compensation under the head of loss of future income.
It is further submitted that the amounts that were granted by the Tribunal on all heads are on higher side and no grounds are made out for enhancement of the compensation.

3 5.
Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
Considering the grievous injury sustained by the claimant, under the head of pain and suffering this court is granting an amount of Rs.40,000/-.

Towards food and nourishment, the court below had granted only an amount of Rs.1,600/-, this court considering the injury to face and the nourishment that is required, this court is granting an amount of Rs.15,000/-.

Then coming to the loss of future income NC: 2023:KHC:46244 due to disability, when it is the case of the claimant that she is earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month, the court below had taken income at Rs.10,000/-
without any basis, as this an accident of the year 2015, this court is taking Rs.9,000/- as income (Rs.9,000/- x 12 x 13 x10/100= 1,40,400/-) is granting an amount of Rs.1,40,400/- under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
Then coming to the loss of income during the laid up period, the court below had rightly granted an amount of Rs.27,000/- and no interference is called for.

Towards medical bills, loss of amenities and future medical expenses, the court below had granted an amount of Rs.3,405/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.20,000/- respectively and the amounts that were granted by the Tribunal for the above three heads are reasonable and no enhancement is required.
However considering the interest aspect, the interest that was granted is at 9% and the same is reduced to 6%.

In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V. MEKALA -vs- M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER 1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.

(b) Respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the said compensation amount with accrued interest before the tribunal within a period of 8 (Eight) weeks.
(c) The amount is deposit shall be forthwith transferred to the court below.
(d) The Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Record to the Tribunal along with the certified copy of the order passed by this court forthwith without any delay.
